findings.title: Likely double-counted matches
findings.detail: Same date and same participants under different IDs. Usually one bout recorded twice (mirrored names, a generic title next to a named one); sometimes a real second bout (a restart, a two-fall match). The old site already leaves 106 matches out of its statistics; each group needs a merge-or-keep decision.
sample: 1998-07-13 Kane, Mankind vs. Billy Gunn, Road Dogg → bulk-match-30846, bulk-match-30849
2000-04-02 Chris Benoit vs. Chris Jericho, Kurt Angle → bulk-match-38637, bulk-match-38638
2001-01-22 Al Snow vs. Raven → bulk-match-41579, bulk-match-41580
2001-09-10 Kurt Angle vs. Rob Van Dam → bulk-match-43125, bulk-match-43126
2002-01-21 William Regal vs. Edge → bulk-match-162973, bulk-match-44000

findings.title: Weekly-show years with fewer than 45 indexed cards
findings.detail: Full years (Raw from 1994, SmackDown from 2000, NXT from 2011, through 2025) where fewer than 45 of roughly 52 episodes have an indexed card. Wave 1 fills these.

findings.title: Same name under different IDs within one scheme
findings.detail: Usually different people who share a ring name, sometimes one person split in two. Review case by case.

findings.title: Gender comes from portrait placeholders
findings.detail: Gender is only recorded as a placeholder image choice (male: 2054, female: 211). The bulk source defaults most people to male, so this needs verification before women's divisions launch.

findings.title: Competitor lists mix teams, members and guests
findings.detail: More competitor names than linked people: team names sit next to their members ("The MFTs", "Solo Sikoa", ...) and some guests have no profile. The new model stores teams as their own records.

findings.title: Card matches missing from career data
findings.detail: Matches on show cards that no career strip shows; 40 have no linked participants at all (for example 2025 women's title matches whose title field holds a single name).

findings.title: Different holders overlapping on one title
findings.detail: Two holders at once. A few are real (unrecognized champions, brand splits), most are date errors.
sample: MLW Caribbean Heavyweight Championship: El Mesías (2021-07-10 to 2022-05-12) overlaps Octagón Jr. (from 2022-03-31)

findings.title: Championship names need one registry
findings.detail: Reigns name 185 distinct titles, but one championship often appears under several spellings; the WWE Championship alone appears as "Undisputed WWE Championship", "/Undisputed WWE Championship", "WWE Championship", "WWE World Heavyweight/WWE Championship", "WWF / WWE Championship". 1 name is malformed (stray punctuation). Migration maps every spelling to one title record with its lineage.

findings.title: One team reign stored once per member
findings.detail: Same title, same start, shared holder. Migration merges each set into one reign with its members.

findings.title: Same name under different ID schemes
findings.detail: A name or alias maps to IDs from different schemes (curated, archive-person, hf-person). Each needs a merge decision before one-ID-per-person.

findings.title: Shows tab lists more episodes than the career data
findings.detail: Episodes in the Shows archive with no record in the main show list (listed without indexed cards). They migrate as shows with coverage "listed only".

findings.title: Same holder, conflicting reign dates
findings.detail: Two records of one holder overlap with different start dates; one of the dates is wrong.

findings.title: Family members without a career link
findings.detail: Of 147 family members, these have no career page link yet; many are historical relatives.

findings.title: Where moment sources point
findings.detail: Top source sites for moments. Records citing only the bulk dataset need an independent source before they count as verified.

logicToPort: PLE detection: app.js marks a show as PLE by category or by a show-name pattern (WrestleMania, SummerSlam, Royal Rumble, ...).

Default roster filter: RAW and SmackDown checked, NXT and AAA unchecked; brands combine with OR.
PWL rating: equal-weight mean of available source scores on a 0–100 scale (matchRatings.method, ratingUI.normalize).
Statistics record sets and the 106 excluded matches (statisticsRecord, statisticsQuality).
Rivalry clustering for feud highlighting (careerRivalries.find / clusters).
Show catalog grouping by promotion and series (showsUI.seriesFor).
